content.comment_body: Hello. I am new to programming, especially with [product_name]. I've been assigned a task to establish Ethernet communication between a [product_name] and a PLC. So far, I haven't succeeded, which is why I'm seeking help here. I've attached some screenshots showing my current configuration. The communication processor I'm using has firmware [version_no], but it's not compatible with my PLC programming software, so I can't install it. Could this be causing my issue, or am I making another mistake? For the variables that [product_name] reads from the PLC program, I am forcing a value via the variable monitor table. Thank you.

Hi, Please check [url] for application examples. There you can find a ready-to-use example for data exchange between [product_name] and a PLC. The example is designed for a PLC with an onboard Ethernet interface. Hope this helps.

Thank you, [user_name]. I've already reviewed those examples—both client and server connection methods—but unfortunately, I was not successful. Do you think the CP firmware could be the issue? As mentioned, my CP firmware is [version_no], but I don't have that version available in my PLC programming software. I will continue reading information and attempting to establish the connection, and will share any results. Any assistance is appreciated. Thanks.

Hello, Please check online to see if the CP is operating. Can you access the CPU via TCP-IP? What version of your programming software do you have? You may be able to locate an HSP for your programming software. Regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], Yes, I can access the CPU through TCP-IP and I can reach [product_name] as well. [product_name] is connected through port 1 of the communication processor, and I use port 2 to connect the programming device, allowing me to see both devices online—the PLC and [product_name]. My programming software version is [version_no]. The HSP for the CP with firmware [version_no] does not seem to be supported by my software. Do you think the issue could be firmware-related? I have a PLC with an integrated PN port, so I will try to establish communication with that, and if it works I'll attribute previous problems to firmware incompatibility. If it still doesn't work, I'll consider it a programming issue. I'll share the results. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is having trouble setting up Ethernet communication between [product_name] and a PLC using programming software [version_no] and a communication processor with firmware [version_no]. They suspect a compatibility issue between the CP firmware and the software version. Although official examples were reviewed, a successful connection has not been established. Both devices are detected on the network, suggesting physical connectivity, but higher-layer communication fails. The user is uncertain about software and firmware compatibility, as well as correct setup procedures.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] and the PLC to communicate reliably over Ethernet through the provided software, even with varying CP firmware versions. They seek clear, straightforward instructions and presume compatibility between hardware and software versions.
